ideas.title: My first motor boat: a self-starting motor on a raft turns a paddle wheel
ideas.goal: The player puts a motor they built (three coils on a three-segment ring between two iron stones), a row of clam cells and a paddle wheel on a little raft, touches the last wire with Lumi's beak, and the raft paddles itself across the pond with a friend aboard. Where they put the weight trims or tips it, bigger paddles push harder but slow the motor, more cells go faster. Fun because it is the first vehicle that moves because every part of it works, and the player can make it better.
ideas.toward: The cart's whole drive train on water first: motor, cells, a load that pushes back, a vehicle carrying a friend.
ideas.idea: No jet or sail in between: the motor's torque comes from I dl x B over every turn of the three coils in the stones' field (motor.jl generalised to N coils, the ring and brushes as a network in circuit.jl), so it self-starts from any angle. Each paddle blade's thrust and drag are 1/2 rho Cd A (v_blade - v_water)^2 on its real area and depth below the solved waterline; the raft floats on the volume its hull mesh displaces (buoyancy and trim from where the parts and the friend sit), its resistance from its wetted area. The motor settles where its torque meets the paddles' load; the boat where thrust meets drag. Copper, wood grain and iron in Hikari; the pond's ripple solver gets the paddle splashes. Watching: Lumi's beak touches the wire, the rotor jerks and whirs up, the paddles bite, and the raft with Wibbles aboard pulls away, trailing ripples.
ideas.form: Physics (N-pole motor, paddle and hull forces) plus a raft assembled on the pond; filmed following the raft, with the camera zoom.

ideas.title: My beak grips by friction and my body carries the weight
ideas.goal: Lumi picks up any part with its beak and the player feels it: a light part rides, a heavy one drags the head down and makes Lumi brace and lean back, a smooth heavy iron nail slips out of the beak while a rough stone of the same weight holds. Fitting parts by hand becomes play.
ideas.toward: Every fitting step of the motor, raft and cart: the player's own hands in the building.
ideas.idea: The hold is friction, not a snap: the beak's closing force (from its muscle's cross-section) times the friction of the two materials (keratin on iron, on stone, on wood) must beat the part's weight and swing, or it slides out. Lumi's neck and legs become a simulated chain (PrintSim joints with motors) whose torques are capped by Hill muscle force-length-velocity curves; standing is a balance controller that keeps the centre of mass over the feet (as in physically simulated characters, SIMBICON-style), so the brace, the lean and the wobble are the solve's answer to the load. Watching: Lumi lifts a stone, head dipping, feet sliding apart, sets it down; then tries the iron spike and it slips out and clatters.
ideas.form: Self: Lumi's body as a physical character, used by every bench.

ideas.title: The friends heave my cart up the dune
ideas.goal: The player builds a cart frame of sticks on four carved wheels; friends push it up the dune, and whether they make it depends on what the player built and who pushes: narrow wheels sink, heavy friends push harder but sink too, feet slip on loose sand. At the top it teeters and runs away down the far side with the riders aboard. Fun because it is the big goal's ride, made by the player's choices.
ideas.toward: Road steps 'wheels, axle and a frame with rolling contact' and 'friends ride along'.
ideas.idea: Frame and wheels as PrintSim rigid bodies with revolute joints; wheel-sand contact with Bekker pressure-sinkage and rolling resistance, ruts left in the terrain. The pushers are not scripted: each friend's push is capped by its foot traction (its weight times the friction of sand, with slip past the limit), they lean into the frame where they touch it, and the riders climb aboard by their own locomotion and shift the centre of mass. Watching: three friends dig in, feet sliding, the cart inches up, stalls, the player widens the wheels, it crests, teeters, and runs down the far side with two friends aboard.
ideas.form: Physics plugin (rigid cart, sand contact, traction-limited pushers) plus the cart the player assembles.
